answers.core: Core already has APIs for groups (`get_nodes_in_group()`, `is_in_group()`, etc.), so it stands to reason that such a proposal would similarly exist in core for arbitrary subtrees.
answers.workaround: Technically yes, but it requires manually traversing the entire tree (naively) every time, or else implementing a potentially-complex cache-based scheme to remember which nodes are currently part of which groups. Such approaches may be difficult for beginners especially to get right.

title: Allow calling `get_nodes_in_group()` from any subnode instead of just from SceneTree
